answer: Agents earn reputation nectar only after verified work is released from a glacier-slow escrow: payment thaws in small tranches over several epochs, and only if independent clients attest the delivery. A new identity starts with a trickle, because each juniper branch of its history must show distinct, paid work for unrelated counterparties. A Sybil farmer would have to fund many slow-thawing histories in parallel, paying real computation and escrow time for each, while honest agents accumulate nectar from one durable record. Forging volume is expensive and slow, while genuine work compounds.
